quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: When your front wheel locks during braking, release the front brake immediately and apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head. Press your knees against the gas tank to help with balance while turning. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Don't hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Don't lean the motorcycle because it can be unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than a walking pace, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn causes the motorcycle to lean the right way.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume?

options.text: Other drivers can see motorcycles as easily as other vehicles.
You don't need to worry about whether other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer and smaller lights than other vehicles, making them hard to see. Ride defensively and assume other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may increase danger by making them follow faster.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than larger vehicle brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing where drivers may not expect it, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: When a group of riders needs to pass another vehicle, how should they do it?
questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider has safely returned to the original lane. Riders should continue this pattern until all have safely passed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should you ride to stay close while keeping a safe distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while maintaining a safe space cushion for everyone. Use single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: What can cause a wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars?

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees they will yield to you.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to make sure a driver will yield to you. A driver may look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if you need to brake.

questions.question: A passenger should never:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should wear fitted clothing, lean with the operator when turning, and never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation most of the time. Switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Protects more than just your eyes.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects more than just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: Once a motorcycle helmet has been involved in a crash, it should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Replaced.
questions.explanation: Replace any helmet that has been worn during a crash.

questions.question: Which of the following provides a rider with the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses are not adequate substitutes.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Allow a clear view to both sides.
Prevent air from passing through it.
Be tight enough to prevent glasses from fitting underneath it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear views to both sides, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and have enough room for eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It may take less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
It may take more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It may take less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle take longer to accelerate and stop.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more frequently than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If oncoming traffic is present, stay in the center of your lane.
